headline: Money rotated out of AI infrastructure into hyperscalers: the semis ETF fell 2.8% (-20.4% on the month) while the S&P rose 1.6%, and grid (-11.0%) and cooling (-12.9%) were hit hardest on Texas data-centre policy fears.
regime: S&P +1.6% and Nasdaq +1.4% on the day, but the semis ETF fell 2.8% and is -11.2% on five days and -20.4% on the month; hyperscalers (+3.1%) were the only segment up. The 10-year eased to 4.89% and crude fell 12.7% on five days, yet the AI-infrastructure complex fell anyway, so rates are no longer the main driver: policy risk after the Democratic sweep and doubts about spending duration are. Every infrastructure segment is down 12-21% on five days; fundamentals (Coherent, Seagate, Modine) are still strong but prices are ignoring them.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Comfort Systems, Quanta and Sterling report record backlogs from AI infrastructure demand (7845c599668e)
Modine data-centre revenue +95% and fiscal 2027 outlook raised to $3.1-3.2bn (66086808ae5c)
Against: grid -11.0% and cooling -12.9% on the day; Eaton fell almost 10% on Q3 despite the results (05c8857708d6)
Against: Vistra hit a 52-week low after Texas elected a governor promising to halt new data centres (af942f1fbb36)
theses.change_note: -6: demand evidence is intact, but the best-priced suppliers are being sold hard on a state-level policy threat, which is a real constraint on demand, not just a price move.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Coherent raised full-year targets, forecasting fiscal 2027 sales up over 60% (e69adcd74ee6)
Seagate: $4.2bn sales and $1.76bn net income in the quarter (d2d5afa4807c)
Against: Microsoft spent less than expected on capex and declined to expand the Nscale Texas lease (ddeb620c05d2, 28189de92c23)
Against: Super Micro stock sank as results exposed cash strain (26a45cb8690f); compute -17.1% on five days
theses.change_note: -6: the largest buyer deferring capacity is the first direct demand-side crack, even though suppliers still print strong numbers.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: Microsoft declined to expand Nscale and a report ties IREN to Microsoft's AI spending delay (28189de92c23, ddeb620c05d2)
CoreWeave under pressure from heavy borrowing and data-centre fears (4ae392809484); CIFR -26.7% on five days
Against: Equinix +4.6% on five days and NextDC +43% on a Digital Realty/Goodman stake show well-funded operators are valued (b0715f993c64)
theses.change_note: +4: the bounce reversed and a hyperscaler pulled back from a leveraged tenant; strong buyers target owners with real cash flow, not borrowers.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Seagate earned $1.76bn on $4.2bn of sales, a very high margin (d2d5afa4807c)
Micron rallied 220% and is called cheap, with the crunch lasting through 2029 (d3b63a85083f)
Against: memory -20.9% on five days and -32.1% on the month, with a Trefis note on a 40% Micron crash risk (e589e83d8e8f)
theses.change_note: -3: earnings are strong but the group keeps falling, so the market is voting for a peak; the margin gap is the only support.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Oracle fell 14% in a week after a $20bn stock and bond sale to fund AI (d9193e973bd3)
Against: Microsoft spent less on capex than expected and gained 4.7% (ddeb620c05d2); hyperscalers +3.1% as money rotated in (29ab672bcb93)
theses.change_note: -4: the market now rewards hyperscalers for spending less, which confirms the cash-flow worry but also means the squeeze is easing at the largest names.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: Semis ETF -20.4% on the month, ai_software -19.3% on five days, with the 10-year at 4.89% (digest tape)
A research firm declares the 'end of the AI trade as we know it' (fac64e2ada09)
Against: the 10-year is falling (-3.0% on five days) and Tom Lee sees a 15-20% tech rally (2f45aee4bc56)
theses.change_note: +2: AI-linked groups fell hard on a day when yields and oil eased, so the weakness is positioning and policy, not just rates.

theses.title: A Democratic Congress and Texas politics raise policy risk for data-centre build-outs
evidence: Texas elected a governor who promised to halt new data centres; Vistra and Vertiv fell to lows (af942f1fbb36)
Steve Weiss says the midterms put a lid on AI spending, with a Texas permit freeze hitting data-centre names (bfc7f3173081)
Marvell fell 7% as the sweep hit data-centre stocks (be8f6bb85a07)
Against: chipmakers barely flinched at first, and Tom Lee expects a tech rally (2f45aee4bc56)
theses.change_note: +18: last session's headline risk is now showing in prices, a Texas permit freeze and a hyperscaler declining Texas capacity.

compute.note: -17.1% on five days, Marvell -36.5%; quality names are cheap but the trend is down.

foundry_equipment.note: -32.2% on the month; fundamentals strong, so buy only quality at a low multiple.

memory_storage.note: -32.1% on the month; Seagate earns heavily but the market prices a peak.

networking_optical.note: Coherent raised targets, yet the group is -34.8% on the month.

servers.note: Super Micro cash strain and Dell -24.6% on five days.

power_nuclear.note: Vistra at a 52-week low on Texas policy; developers still burn cash.

grid_electrical.note: Record contractor backlogs, but -11.0% on the day; Hubbell flat on five days.

cooling_thermal.note: -12.9% on the day despite Modine's +95% data-centre revenue; policy fear dominates.

datacenter_neocloud.note: Microsoft declined Nscale expansion; funding stress and the cash-flow gate remain.

hyperscalers.note: Relief bounce (+3.1%) on lower capex, but Oracle's funding strain persists.

risks: State or federal data-centre limits (Texas permit freeze) could delay orders across power, grid and cooling.
Microsoft's capex restraint may spread to other hyperscalers and cut supplier growth.
Leveraged neoclouds could lose financing and strand GPU and power orders.
Semis are -20% on the month; further forced selling could drag even the strong balance sheets.
Oil and the Iran war remain a black swan for inflation and rates.
watch: Whether grid and cooling stabilise after a -11% to -13% day or the selling continues.
Any Texas legislation, permit rules or copycat state moratoria.
Capex commentary from other hyperscalers after Microsoft's under-spend.
Nebius earnings on Nov. 12 and neocloud financing news.
The semis ETF against -20% on the month and the 10-year at 4.89%.
